mina: heads up — after swapping in the new vectorized pos-enc kernel selector yesterday we started seeing tiny numerical regressions on long sequences (>2048). not full outages, but a handful of NaNs and diffs in gen outputs. investigating. :eyes:

samir: can you paste the logs / stack traces? which kernel path landed (ROPE vs ALiBi)?

mina: logs attached below — selector picked the optimized fused ROPE kernel for fp16 on A100s. failures only when seq_len grows and kv cache re-use happens across batches. infra-bot reported 12 NaN events in the last 30m.

jess: pasted kernel traceback: ```
E floating point exception at posenc_fused.cu:142
kernel: fused_rope_apply(fp16, seq=4096, bsz=8, head=64)
stack: fastpath->apply_rope->fused_rope_apply
```

liam: hmm — we saw similar when the quantized int8 path hit accumulation overflow. are we mixing fp16 accumulation with int8 dequant in the fused path?

mina: yes — selector allowed int8-dequant + fp16-accum fused kernel for speed. suspected cause: rounding + accumulation order causes outliers for large seq.

samir: two angles: (1) short-term mitigation — change selector heuristics to avoid fused path for seq_len > 2048 or when quantized path is active; (2) long-term — refactor posenc interface so ALiBi/ROPE implementations expose a stable reference and a fast-but-guarded opt-in.

jess: agree. also noticed we lack golden reference comparisons in CI for pos-enc differences. current unit tests only check shape and dtype. we need numerical regression tests.

mina: proposal: implement a PosEncAdapter interface in runtime with methods: `precompute(context)`, `apply_kv(qkv, cache, seq_offset)`, `verify_against_ref(input, ref_fp64)` and wire selector to consult adapter.capabilities (stable_fast, quantized_safe, max_seq_len). then update kernel selector rules to prefer `stable_fast` when workload crosses quantization/seq thresholds.

liam: sounds reasonable. for immediate hotfix I can flip selector rule: `if seq_len>=2048 or quantized_path: route->stable_reference_kernel`. low risk.

jess: test plan for refactor:
1) add a python fuzz harness that generates random seq lengths (1..8192), heads, batch sizes, random weights/inputs and compares `fast_kernel` vs `ref_fp64` with tolerances: abs_diff < 1e-3 for fp16 fused, and no NaNs.
2) add nightly stress job that runs high-seq scenarios on dedicated A100 nodes with bf16 and fp16.
3) add telemetry: `posenc_nans`, `posenc_max_absdiff`, `posenc_kernel_choice` tags. fail CI if fuzz finds NaNs.

mina: here's a quick fuzz snippet to drop into eng-ml/test_harness: ```python
import numpy as np
def fuzz_once(seq, heads, bsz, dtype):
    ref = compute_rope_ref(input.astype(np.float64))
    out_fast = fused_rope_apply(input.astype(dtype))
    maxdiff = np.max(np.abs(out_fast.astype(np.float64)-ref))
    assert not np.isnan(out_fast).any(), 'nan in fast path'
    assert maxdiff < 1e-3, f'maxdiff {maxdiff}'
```

samir: add also a tiny deterministic seed and edge-cases set: seq=1, seq=2, seq=1024, seq=2048, seq=4096, odd head dims, huge batch with small heads. gotchas around wrap/rotation boundaries for ROPE.

liam: rollout plan for the hotfix: 1) patch selector in canary branch, 2) run fuzz harness in CI + manual pump of generated traffic against staging, 3) deploy canary with 1% production traffic on Dedicated for 6h, monitor telemetry, increase to 10% if clean, full rollout after 24h. rollback path: flip selector back to old rule and redeploy.

jess: assignable TODOs: mina — open RFC for PosEncAdapter (include interface and selector mapping). samir — add CI fuzz job and golden FP64 reference runner. liam — push selector hotfix PR and coordinate canary. i'll add telemetry metrics and dashboards.

mina: created RFC draft: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/posenc-adapter (WIP). added section on numeric guarantees and permissible epsilon for each dtype.

infra-bot: deploy-check triggered for branch "posenc/selector-hotfix" — all tests passed. :white_check_mark:

mina: thanks — can we also add a guard in the fused kernel itself: clamp intermediate accumulators, detect NaN/inf and fallback to reference in-kernel? that might be more robust than selector-only approach.

liam: in-kernel fallback would cost perf but is safest. we should implement a cheap post-check: after accumulation do `if (isnan(acc) || abs(acc)>1e6) goto fallback;` and have fallback call the stable scalar kernel. doable but need careful CUDA synchronization.

samir: prefer selector + CI + telemetry first to limit blast radius, then follow up with in-kernel guard as an additional safety net.

jess: also watch ALiBi slope computation — we had an earlier PR that optimized the slope math with single-precision reciprocal, which accumulated error for long sequences. make sure reference covers that.

mina: agreed. i'll add ALiBi slope unit tests and cross-check with long seq reference.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: 1% traffic -> dedicated-us-east-1-d-01. monitoring window 6h.

mina: thanks team. i'll track RFC + tests. follow-ups: add ticket to eng-runtime backlog for in-kernel guard, and schedule a 30m sync after canary window. :+1:

liam: ping me once canary metrics are up, i'll be standing by to revert if anything spikes.

samir: awesome. one more note — let's version the selector decisions in telemetry (selector_v=...) so we can correlate regressions with selector rules.

jess: will add selector_v and kernel_variant tags to all posenc metrics.

mina: closing thread for now, will post updates here after canary. :rocket:
